meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Kingdom of Spain; unitary national jurisdiction with no separate tax-registering sub-state distinction for SL incorporation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 2005; entered into force 2008)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended (in particular by Ley 11/2021, transposing EU Directives 2018/843 and 2018/1673); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the implementing Reglamento and creating the notarial beneficial-ownership register (Registro de Titularidad Real); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 9 and 198 on registered office and shareholders ledger; Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) as applicable to UBO data processing.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (access is limited to competent authorities, SEPBLAC, the General Council of the Notariat, obliged financial institutions, notaries, lawyers and corporate service providers acting for AML customer-due-diligence purposes; no general public access after ECJ Case C-37/20 of 22 November 2022)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial certification of identity and legal capacity of each non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner (certified passport extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority or notary public in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention of 5 October 1961; consular legalization at the Spanish Embassy or Consulate for non-member jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: General or special Power of Attorney granted to the incorporator for execution of the SL constitution deed and NIF application
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or Spanish Consul

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence and good standing of any legal-person shareholder or parent holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country commercial registry or companies registrar

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference or statement evidencing source of funds and availability of capital for the statutory contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's bank of origin or the Spanish bank issuing the blocked-capital certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and corporate compliance form (declaración de titularidad real) with layered ownership/nominee/trust piercing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary and Consejo General del Notariado (Registro de Titularidad Real)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial instrument; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Ley 10/2010, Articles 11-15: full identification and verification of each UBO and politically exposed person (domestic, EU and international PEP lists per SEPBLAC criteria); screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014, Council Regulation (EU) 2580/2001, and, where USD clearing or a US nexus exists, the OFAC SDN List; enhanced due diligence required for high-risk third countries identified by FATF; all screening evidence and customer files retained for ten years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) telematic denomination certificate service, electronically accessible through the Ministry of Justice official platform and the RMC portal (rmc.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The denominación social must be composed in Spanish or in any co-official language of the Spanish State, written in Latin script; foreign-language names are accepted only when transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied, where necessary, by a non-misleading Spanish rendering; the corporate suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' is mandatory and cannot be omitted or translated.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or phonetically/orthographically coincident with any already registered or pre-reserved Spanish company denomination
Terms implying State, royal or official status: 'España', 'Estado', 'Gobierno', 'Ministerio', 'Real', 'Nacional', 'Público'
Financial-sector reserved tokens requiring prior supervisory authorization: 'Banco', 'Caja', 'Seguro', 'Bolsa', 'Inversión' in a misleading context
Misleading terms suggesting administrative, regulated or professional activity for which the company does not hold a license
Titles incorporating identifiable natural persons without express consent, or expressions contrary to public order or good customs
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC negative name certificate (certificado negativo de denominación) expires automatically after 180 days from issuance; there is no administrative extension, but a fresh telematic application may be filed once the name becomes available again. Upon rejection (certificado positivo, coincidence, or refusal), the applicant may file a written reconsideration (recurso de reposición) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of notification, followed, if necessary, by a contentious-administrative appeal before the Audiencia Nacional within two months. As a practical parallel remedy, the applicant may immediately re-file a batch of three alternative denominations through the RMC electronic service to avoid procedural delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-office or mailbox address does not satisfy Article 9 of the Spanish Capital Companies Act (real-seat doctrine: the SL must have its registered office in Spain at the place where effective administration is located or where the principal establishment operates). For the present smart-meter manufacturing scope, a physical registered office and industrial plant are required for municipal permits, industrial licensing, and AEAT substance verification; a virtual address may serve only as a supplementary correspondence point.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-trivial: approximately 3% annual probability of unannounced AEAT on-site substance verification during NIF/VAT registration and post-incorporation review, plus separate municipal and environmental inspections once the plant is operational; prudent to maintain signed leases, payroll records, utility bills and inventory logs on site.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 4 (minimum capital), 19 to 29 (public deed, incorporation formalities and registration), 5 (registered office), 105 and 128 (single director), 209 to 214 (share capital); Commercial Registry Regulation (Real Decreto 1784/1996).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for name clearance and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for inscription; supervisory authority is the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministerio de Justicia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) executed before a Spaniard notary, followed by mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil and issuance of the provisional NIF (tax identification number) by the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum subscribed and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 3,000 for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, pursuant to Article 4.1 LSC. Cash contributions must be deposited into a Spanish credit institution in the name of the company before deed execution and evidenced by an unconditional bank certificate (certificado de desembolso); non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report. The immobilized deposit is released only after inscription in the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], S.L. In Madrid, on [DATE], the founding members unanimously adopt the following resolutions: (1) The entire share capital of EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 equal participations of EUR 1.00 nominal value each, is subscribed and fully paid-up as evidenced by the bank deposit certificate attached to the deed. (2) The registered office is established at [ADDRESS], Spain, and the legal representatives are instructed to file all statutory registrations. (3) [FULL NAME] is appointed Sole Administrator (Administrador Único) with full powers of management and representation in accordance with Articles 105 and 128 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital. All resolutions pass unanimously and shall be incorporated into the public deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance (Certificación Negativa de Denominación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Ministerio de Justicia, Madrid — online via the Central Registry electronic office or through any provincial commercial registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a formal application proposing up to three alternative corporate names for an SL. The Central Registry verifies that the proposed name does not coincide with or resemble an existing undertaking. Once issued, the negative name certificate is valid for three non-renewable months and must be attached to the notarial deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Application form for name certificate (formulario de certificación de denominación)
Passport or NIE photostat of each founding member
List of one to three proposed corporate names in order of priority
Proof of payment of the Central Registry filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for identity or phonetic resemblance with an existing name, immediately file a new application with alternate names; each re-application requires a fresh fee but can be completed electronically within two working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Corporate Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Banco de España.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000. Obtain an unconditional bank certificate of deposit identifying the depositors, the company name, IBAN, amount and date. This certificate is mandatory evidence of the full payment of the subscribed capital before the notary, unless a notarized bank guarantee is substituted.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of each promoter and proposed director
Draft articles of association (borrador de estatutos)
Anti-money laundering declaration of final beneficial owners (declaración de titularidad real)
Negative name certificate issued by Registro Mercantil Central
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC information, supply source-of-funds documentation and beneficial ownership evidence; a bank refusal may be overcome by choosing an alternative bank or by having the notary certify a non-cash contribution in lieu of cash deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation before a Spanish Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary belonging to the Ilustre Colegio Notarial of the chosen city, subject to the Ministerio de Justicia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members must appear in person or through a duly empowered attorney before the notary to execute the Escritura de Constitución. The deed integrates the name certificate, the full articles of association, the capital deposit certificate, and the first board resolution. The notary submits the deed for settlement of the Impuesto sobre Actos Jurídicos Documentados (AJD) to the regional tax office and issues certified copies for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate still in force
Bank certificate of full capital deposit
NIE or passport of each subscriber, translated and apostilled if foreign
Approved draft articles of association
Modelo 600 or regional AJD self-assessment form where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects a statutory defect or formal irregularity, the founders sign an addendum or a new deed correcting the inconsistency; minor reserves are curable through a notarial act of rectification without restarting the formation timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — via the Sede Electrónica or the AEAT corporate assistance desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after execution of the deed, submit form 036 (censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) together with a certified copy of the public deed and the first board resolution. The AEAT registers the company on the Spanish tax census and assigns a provisional NIF valid for six months, which becomes definitive only after completion of licensing and full tax census duties.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036, signed by the legal representative
Certified copy of the public deed of incorporation
NIE or DNI of the appointed legal representative
Bank capital deposit certificate (testimonio bancario)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT issues a request for rectification, the administrator has 10 working days, per Article 68 of Law 39/2015, to cure the omission; a fresh application after correction is processed within three working days without penalties if timely submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office, under the supervision of the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary, or the administrator, files the first copy of the deed (primer testimonio) together with the first board resolution for registration within one month of execution. The registrar verifies legality, capacity and formal correctness of the deed and the corporate governance acts. Upon registration, the company acquires full legal personality and the administrator obtains a literal registration certification for banking, licensing and contractual purposes.
required_dossiers: Notarial first-copy deed of incorporation (primer testimonio)
First board resolution duly approved and inserted
Provisional NIF certificate
Instancia (registration request) signed by the administrator
Payment of the registry tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a nota de suspensión for a defect, the administrator corrects the defect and requests re-entry of the deed; a denial can be appealed before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within 15 days of service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security Enrollment and Post-Incorporation Corporate Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the TGSS (inscripción de empresa) and communicate the administrator's appointment, together with the opening of a payroll account system. Legalize the official corporate books (libro de actas, libro registro de socios and registro de participaciones) at the Commercial Registry and adopt the compulsory corporate e-address and company website data publication infolores before the Registry.
required_dossiers: Certification of inscription issued by Registro Mercantil Provincial
Definitive NIF certificate
Modelo TA.6 company enrollment form (inscripción de empresa)
Officer appointment communication form (Modelo TA.1 or SL)
Corporate books to be legalized (libros obligatorios)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TGSS rejects or queries the enrollment, re-submit the complete file through the RED/SILTRA online system; any outstanding social security arrears can be settled to lift the certificate hold, and the Commercial Registry accepts a remedial presentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria of the competent Autonomous Community, and the municipal licensing department of the city where the manufacturing plant is located (technical services for the Licencia de Apertura).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura del Establecimiento Industrial (municipal opening licence for classified activity) combined with the Declaration or Communication of Industrial Establishment Opening under Royal Decree 559/2010; where applicable, a Ley 21/1992 Industrial Activities Authorization may be required for plants exceeding hazardous thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO); regional environmental authority of the Autonomous Community.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: not subject to full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) under Annex I of Law 21/2013; only a simplified environmental assessment (evaluación de impacto ambiental simplificada) may be required for installations above Annex II thresholds (e.g., large production areas). Non-threshold smart-meter assembly plants typically require only a municipal environmental classification (licencia ambiental / calificación ambiental, Class II or III) subject to integrated waste, noise, and wastewater conditions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to municipal sewers must meet municipal by-law limits and generally not exceed COD 500 mg/L, BOD5 300 mg/L, suspended solids 300 mg/L, and pH 6.0-9.0; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from soldering, coating or conformal coating must comply with Royal Decree 117/2003 (EU Directive 1999/13/EC), including solvent management plans; waste electrical and electronic equipment must be managed as WEEE per Royal Decree 110/2015 and Law 7/2022; RoHS substance restrictions apply per Royal Decree 219/2013; no hazardous solvent usage above 0.5 tonnes/year without prior notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety conformity and maintenance certificate per the RIPCI (Royal Decree 513/2017); structural soundness certificate issued by a qualified architect or engineer for the production floor and any mezzanine; low-voltage electrical installation certificate per REBT (Royal Decree 842/2002); occupational risk prevention assessment and planning under Law 31/1995, covering emergency exits, machine safeguarding, racking safe-load inspection, and workplace noise exposure limits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Ministry of Finance; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; business/VAT census and non-resident NIF procedures are handled through AEAT offices and the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Spanish SL, the notary first requests a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for the company from AEAT before executing the public deed; after registration in the Mercantile Registry, the final NIF is issued and serves as the Spanish VAT identification number. A foreign entity acting directly without a Spanish PE/SL must apply for a non-resident NIF by filing Form 030 or 036, as applicable, with certified constitutional documents, proof of foreign tax residence, and appointment of a tax representative if the entity is established outside the EU/EEA; direct VAT registration is made via Form 036 or the EU OSS portal where applicable. Registration must be completed before any taxable supply is made or any Spanish invoice is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a check-the-box or unilateral entity classification election; a Spanish SL is automatically a separate taxable person for Corporate Income Tax under Ley 27/2014 and for VAT under Ley 37/1992. Available elections relevant here: (i) optional consolidated corporate tax group regime under article 58 LIS for qualifying resident subsidiaries with 75%/70% ownership; (ii) special VAT simplified regime and recargo de equivalencia for small retailers below legal turnover ceilings; (iii) OSS non-Union/EU VAT schemes for qualifying intra-EU distance sales and certain digital/B2C services; (iv) optional ETVE international holding regime; (v) no hybrid mismatch election remains available after ATAD implementation via Law 4/2021.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish Value Added Tax); the Canary Islands uses IGIC and Ceuta/Melilla use IPSI, but peninsular manufacturing operations are subject to IVA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general Spanish registration threshold: any person habitually carrying out taxable supplies in Spanish VAT territory must register from the first taxable transaction. The main relevant thresholds are the EU-wide distance-selling/OSS threshold of EUR 10,000 for intra-EU remote sales and the import-OSS scheme; non-EU suppliers of electronic, telecom and broadcasting services to Spanish consumers are taxable in Spain with no registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain imposes no nationwide real-time fiscal pre-clearance for all taxpayers. Mandatory elements: (i) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires large companies and certain VAT groups to transmit invoice records and ledger entries to AEAT by web service/API in XML within four business days of issuance; (ii) Verifactu (RD 1007/2023) requires billing software to guarantee invoice integrity, traceability and legibility with standardised XML/QR/hash records retained and accessible to AEAT; (iii) B2B e-invoicing between businesses is being phased in under Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) using Facturae/EN16931 formats; (iv) invoicing the public sector mandates Facturae format; (v) TicketBAI is a mandatory real-time digital stamping and hash-chain invoice system in the Basque provinces and certain foral territories.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods outside the EU/Spain's customs territory are exempt with entitlement to deduct input VAT, effectively applying 0% VAT, when the goods leave Spain within the statutory exit window and are evidenced by the export declaration and departure certificate. Intra-Community supplies to another EU taxable person may be zero-rated if the purchaser's valid EU VAT ID and transport evidence are held. B2B services supplied to a business established outside Spain are generally not subject to Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rules in articles 69-70 LIVA; however, services connected to Spanish real estate or physically performed in Spain may remain taxable even if the recipient is non-EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/electronic SAD) with export reference number and date
Bill of Lading, air waybill, CMR or certificate of departure evidencing physical exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank payment/FX repatriation evidence linked to the export invoice
Proof of the customer's identity/VAT registration where relevant for intra-Community supply
Certificado de salida or AEAT electronic exit record evidencing export completion
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT closely audits export exemptions; where export evidence is incomplete, payment trace is impossible, or exit is not timely proven, zero-rating is denied and output VAT is clawed back at 21%, with late-payment interest and penalties. Infractions involving false, incomplete or deceptive export records are treated as grave offenses under articles 191-193 LGT, with penalty scales generally 50% to 100%, and up to 150% where concealment or recidivism exists. Supplying fake export invoices to third parties may also trigger criminal tax fraud liability under article 305 of Ley Orgánica 10/1995 when defrauded tax in any tax period exceeds EUR 120,000, with imprisonment terms. Repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days is a commercial and documentary-evidence expectation rather than a standalone VAT exemption condition; however, inconsistent inward remittance can undermine the commercial substance of the export and provoke clawback, denial of refunds, and future audit exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem as the national central bank and as the Spanish foreign exchange and payments supervisor, in coordination with the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business) for capital movement, foreign direct investment declaration and export receipt statistical compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a full member of the Eurozone: the euro (EUR) is the sole legal tender and there is complete convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC. No Spanish exchange-control approval is required for trade payments, dividend or profit remittance, repayment of intercompany loans, or liquidation distributions, provided the SL has complied with corporate and tax legislation. Profit remittance hurdles are predominantly tax-side: the SL must settle its corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), withhold and deposit the 19% non-resident withholding tax on dividends and interest (reducible under the applicable Double Tax Treaty and, for EU residents, under Directive 2011/96/EU), and submit the annual Modelo 720 declaration if any foreign financial assets exceed EUR 50,000 in aggregate. Banking-side compliance includes the completion of balance-of-payments (BOP) statistical declarations to the Banco de España for cross-border payments and the foreign investment ex-post declaration for direct investments from non-EU counterparties, as required under Royal Decree 571/2001 and Law 19/2003, as amended by the investment-screening regime introduced by Royal Decree-Law 34/2020 and Law 8/2023.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio and no obligation to repatriate export receivables. Exporters of smart electricity meters and IoT telemetry sensors (ISIC 2651) may freely hold export proceeds in EUR, USD, CNY or other currencies in domestic multi-currency accounts or offshore accounts. Residual obligations are reporting-driven: (i) export settlements must support the BOP statistical declaration and, when requested by the receiving bank, must be accompanied by the applicable purpose code (código de finalidad) and a copy of the export Single Administrative Document (SAD) and the commercial invoice; (ii) an annual Modelo 720 declaration is mandatory if aggregate balances of foreign accounts or dispositive rights exceed EUR 50,000; and (iii) where export financing is drawn from a Spanish credit institution, the bank may contractually require assignment or pledging of export proceeds, though this is a private contractual matter and not a statutory conversion rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/CNY)
Operational Current Account with Trade Finance and Swift LC Desk
Operational Account and Project Milestone Wire Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a secondary treasury sweep rail; Low as a primary capital escrow or documentary credit rail. Spanish and passporting electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Wise, Payoneer Europe, N26 Bank) operate under Law 21/2011 and the European EBA e-money regime but cannot issue commercial letters of credit, cannot execute confirmed forward FX with a settlement counterparty, and have no direct TARGET2 participation. They are legally viable for euro-denominated operational disbursements, SEPA and SWIFT-governed international payments, and sub-account treasury visibility, but the SL must anchor its capital escrow, project milestone wires and Swift LC rail at a Tier-1 commercial bank. The SL should also audit EMI contractual restrictions on fund usage, payment screening engines for IoT hardware transactions, and operational caps before routing supplier payments through an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto mandatory. Under Spanish AML law (Law 10/2010, as amended by Law 6/2023), Spanish Tier-1 banks require the legal representative of a newly incorporated SL to attend an in-person compliance interview at the branch before account activation; remote video identification is not accepted for an industrial company with critical-infrastructure exposure and high-value cross-border flows. A non-resident director may delegate through a notarized power-of-attorney (poder notarial), apostilled under the Hague Convention and translated into Spanish by a sworn translator, but the attorney-in-fact must still physically attend the branch presenting the original deed and a valid passport, DNI or NIE. In practice, fully digital account opening is available only for low-risk natural-person accounts; for the ES_SL structure, at least one physical visit by a director or authorized attorney-in-fact is unavoidable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain incorporating Panama, BVI, or other offshore holding layers that obscure the ultimate shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Registro Mercantil Central extract of the entire shareholding chain, UBO declaration filed with the Registro de Titularidades Reales, audited group organisational chart, notarized declaration of economic substance in each holding jurisdiction, tax residence certificates of each intermediate entity, and a sworn Spanish translation of all corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU parent capital contribution flagged as foreign direct investment in critical infrastructure (smart grid hardware / ISIC 2651), triggering pre-authorization scrutiny under the Spanish foreign investment screening regime.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authorization or non-opposition file from the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones where the target provides critical services; the notification filed with the Registro de Inversiones under Royal Decree 571/2001; the share subscription agreement; the Spanish notarial deed of capital increase; and the bank certificate of deposit (certificado de desembolso) showing the actual EUR disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward capital injection or milestone wire received from an unrelated third party or routed through a non-banking intermediary without documented commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized underlying purchase or manufacturing agreement, commercial invoice, bill of lading or air waybill with customs import summary, pre-advised SWIFT MT103 message reference, purpose field coordinated with the receiving account banker, and a month-ahead treasury forecast so the bank can pre-clear the expected wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid, high-velocity trade disbursements to diverse supplier jurisdictions including China, Chile, Mexico and the UAE that are disproportionate to the SL's declared payroll and operating cost base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segmented PO-invoice-B/L matching ledger, standardized SWIFT purpose codes for machinery and component import settlements, supplier onboarding CDD files held at the Trade Finance desk, a full transfer-pricing file under Article 16 bis of Law 27/2014, and a formal treasury policy letter signed by the Chief Executive or Managing Director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Smart-meter and IoT manufacturer flagged for dual-use telecommunications exposure and for supplying state-owned grid operators in certain foreign markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid industrial operating license from the competent Ministry or regional authority; IEC 62056/DLMS-COSEM certificate; ISO 27001 certificate; ENS (Esquema Nacional de Seguridad) compliance report; end-user attestation or end-user certificate (EUC) confirming non-sensitive use; a restricted-export compliance manual validated by counsel; and the dual-use assessment or license under EU Regulation 2021/821 where the product falls within dual-use Annex I or II.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing for the inbound capital injection into the ES_SL is a bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer in EUR (with a matching MT202 cover from the remitter's correspondent) directed to the SL's capital escrow or operational account at a Tier-1 Spanish bank. The transfer must be pre-announced through the bank's corporate treasury advisory desk, must be settled in EUR or converted at the receiving bank's internal FX desk from USD or CNY at a disclosed spot or forward rate, and must state an unambiguous commercial purpose in SWIFT field 70 (e.g., 'APORTACION CAPITAL SOCIAL', 'ESCROW CAPITAL SHARE SUBSCRIPTION', or 'LOAN DISBURSEMENT FROM NON-RESIDENT SHAREHOLDER'). Prior to drawdown, the SL must verify whether the investment is subject to foreign investment authorization, verification or post-declaration procedure under Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree 571/2001; the competent register is the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores managed by the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio. The beneficiary bank will independently complete a BOP purpose-code submission to the Banco de España and will reject cash deposits, cryptocurrency-funded transfers, credit-card-funded disbursements, or transfers from unlicensed money transmitters or non-bank intermediaries. Settlement timing is same-day for SEPA and EUR-cleared payments, and 1-3 business days for non-EUR corridors depending on correspondent banking latency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for smart meter components and IoT sensor procurement are executed through the following clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers (telegraphic transfers against documentary invoice) for advance payments and milestone triggers to suppliers in China, the EU and Latin America; (ii) irrevocable commercial Letters of Credit (Swift LC) issued under ICC UCP 600 and eUCP with SWIFT MT700 issuance for larger project milestone disbursements and for suppliers requiring secured payment against complying shipping documents; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) for euro-denominated operational payments to EU counterparties; (iv) SEPA Instant Credit Transfers (SCT Inst) capped at EUR 100,000 per payment for urgent intra-EU disbursements; and (v) documentary collections (documents against payment D/P and documents against acceptance D/A) as a lower-cost alternative to LC for trusted suppliers. FX-denominated disbursements in USD or CNY are covered by the bank's internal FX desk with an executed spot or forward trade. The SL must attach the underlying invoice, purchase order and transport document to any payment instruction above the bank's AML threshold, commonly EUR 10,000, and must ensure that all China, Chile and Mexico related payments are priced at arm's length under the transfer-pricing rules of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (Law 27/2014) to avoid tax non-deductibility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contracts (Seguro de Cambio) in EUR/USD, EUR/CNY and EUR/MXN executed with a Tier-1 Spanish credit institution under ISDA documentation and MiFID II suitability, covering committed trade payables and project milestone inflows.
Vanilla FX Options (European-style calls and puts) in EUR/USD and EUR/CNY, with premium paid upfront, hedging budgeted procurement volumes without ongoing mark-to-market obligations.
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) between EUR and USD or EUR and CNY for intercompany shareholder loans and long-maturity trade facilities where the SL has offsetting receivable and payable flows.
FX Swaps (spot-forward linked transactions, including tom/next and overnight rollovers) for short-term Treasury liquidity repositioning on the multi-currency account platform.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market supplier currencies with restricted convertibility, limited to genuine underlying trade exposure and executed on a margin-backed basis with a French, UK or Spanish bank counterparty that has restricted-currency booking capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit and Annual UBO Declaration (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales y Declaración de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry of the corporate seat (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year SLs must file by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Graduated administrative fine of €1,200 to €6,000 under art. 283 Ley de Sociedades de Capital; persistent non-deposit triggers closure of the registry file and administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Form 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months and 25 days after fiscal year-end; calendar-year taxpayers due by 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 5% (within 3 months) escalating to 20% (after 12 months) of tax due, plus statutory late interest; substantive penalties of 50%–150% of the omitted amount; AEAT may compel filing and have activities suspended.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Registro de Titulares Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titulares Reales of the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the deposit of annual accounts, within six months after fiscal year-end; notifiable changes must be submitted within ten business days of the notarial share deed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML infringement under Ley 10/2010: fines of €1,000 to €10,000, or up to double the economic benefit obtained; repeat breach may also result in registry file closure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory when the SL exceeds at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets > €2,845,000; net annual turnover > €5,700,000; average staff > 50. Audit is also required for financial, credit, insurance and listed entities, regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, Real Decreto 1514/2007) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used by consolidated groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must annually declare all ultimate beneficial owners holding at least 25% of shares or voting rights, directly or indirectly, and update any shareholding transfers during the fiscal year. Share transfers must be notarized and filed with the Mercantile Registry before the annual UBO declaration is accepted if registration validity is to be preserved.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 25% statutory rate. Qualifying newly-created Spanish companies obtain 15% on the first EUR 300,000 of positive tax base for up to two tax periods; certified start-ups under Law 28/2022 may apply 15% for up to four tax periods. Additional relief includes participation exemption of 95% for foreign dividends/capital gains under qualifying shareholdings, R&D and technological innovation tax credits, the patent box regime for qualifying intangible income, and double-taxation relief through tax treaties. Tax losses are offset without a hard statutory expiry but are subject to turnover-based quantitative limits (60%, 50%, or 25% of positive tax base) and a minimum EUR 1 million offset allowance.
